sessions.description:
We begin with introductions. Who are you? Do you have a favourite poet?
I'll then talk briefly about the life and work of William Blake.
Together we'll read aloud a cluster of the very short Songs of Innocence. Before carefully analysing four of them, we'll do a bit of class writing. After reading another cluster of six - we take a short break.

Now we look closely at Blake's visual designs. Are there any patterns? Does that influence our analysis of at least three more poems?

We continue our Innocence journey, reading aloud. And then we play a poetry game, creating group poems before returning to Blake. How do nature, culture, and the divine intermingle? How important is empathy? What is the value of Innocence? Can you see with the eyes of your heart?

After the break, we enter into Experience. What has changed? Carefully, we explore at least four poems.

We continue in Experience. How do the 'companion poems' ('Infant Joy'/'Infant Sorrow'; 'The Chimney Sweeper[s]; 'The Lamb' & 'The Tyger') interrelate? Can you be in a state of Innocence when in Experience?

In our first hour we continue in Experience. We read, write creatively, and critically analyse. Then we regain innocent wisdom in Blake's "Auguries of Innocence."

After the break, we feast poetically. You'll each be asked to read a short Arabic poem, perhaps one you have written. Translation can be enjoyable. How does poetic beauty deepen perception? How can your favourite poetry be 'in conversation' with William Blake's?

bibliography.title: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
